title: O Lord, My God, I Cry to Thee
description: O Lord, My God, I Cry to Thee in Tonic Solfa to MELITA, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Nikolaus Selnecker wrote these words in German. Catherine Winkworth's translation was printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 543.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre, six lines (8.8.8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELITA; any other Long Metre, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: O Lord, my God, I cry to Thee, In my dis-tress Thou hel-pest me. My soul and bo-dy I com-mend In-to Thy hands; Thine an-gel send To guide me home and cheer my heart Since Thou dost call me to de-part.

lines: O Lord, my God, I cry to Thee,
In my distress Thou helpest me.
My soul and body I commend
Into Thy hands; Thine angel send
To guide me home and cheer my heart
Since Thou dost call me to depart.
O Jesus Christ, Thou Lamb of God,
Once slain to take away our load,
Now let Thy cross, Thine agony,
Avail to save and solace me;
Thy death to open heaven and there
Bid me the joy of angels share.
O Holy Spirit, at the end,
Sweet Comforter, be Thou my Friend,
When death and hell assail me sore,
Leave me, O leave me nevermore,
But bear me safely through the strife,
As Thou hast promised, into life.

licence: Public domain: Nikolaus Selnecker died in 1592; Catherine Winkworth died in 1878.
credits: Words by Nikolaus Selnecker (1530–1592), translated by Catherine Winkworth (1827–1878), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to MELITA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
